goal: Decide which front end feature each stakeholder sees for each part of an answer, so every view shows what that reader needs and nothing that buries it.

app.name: frontend-feature
app.title: Front end feature
app.purpose: Decide, as a DMN decision table with hit policy FIRST, which front end feature renders one surface of an answer (the answer, its reason, its rules, its proof, the journey, the words or the seal) for a stakeholder viewpoint, or that the surface is not shown in that view.
limits: It decides what is shown; the backend capability that serves each feature is decided by backend-capability.
The words inside a feature come from the product record, prism/product.json.

fields.name: viewpoint
fields.means: the stakeholder viewpoint the reader chose: platform, cloud, operator, security, leader or business

fields.name: surface
fields.means: the part of an answer to render: the answer itself, its plain reason, the rules that fired, the proof, the journey of checked examples, the UOR words, or the holo seal

meanings.verdict-card: the one-word answer, coloured by whether it is positive, negative or a refusal
meanings.plain-reason: one sentence in the reader's words: why this answer, and which promise it keeps
meanings.rule-trace: the rule that fired, its conditions and the spec line it cites
meanings.proof-panel: the property theorems, where they live, and the CI run that checked them
meanings.journey-steps: the reader's journey as checked examples they can replay one by one
meanings.lexicon-panel: the UOR term, its platform term and its plain words, side by side
meanings.seal-badge: the holo fingerprint and the replayed acceptance vectors, shown before any answer
meanings.not-shown: this surface is left out of this view, so it does not bury the answer

rules.why: every reader is shown the seal before trusting an answer: verify before you trust
every view leads with the answer
every view gives the reason in its own words
every view can translate a UOR word into its platform word
every view has a journey of checked examples
a leader decides go, hold or no-go and is not handed protocol rules
a business owner weighs cost and loss, not protocol rules
a leader gets the promise in plain words, with the proof one link away
a business owner gets the promise in plain words
an engineer sees the rule that fired and the spec line it cites
an engineer sees the theorems and the run that checked them

app.otherwiseWhy: a surface no rule places is left out

properties.why: a leader is never handed protocol rules
every reader in every view sees the seal
every view leads with the answer

stakeholders.name: Engineering leader
stakeholders.text: Decides whether a platform change ships and needs the answer and its reason, never a wall of protocol detail.
concerns: Each view shows only what its reader needs

stakeholders.name: Platform engineer
stakeholders.text: Builds the platform and wants the rule that fired and the theorem behind it one click from the answer.

stakeholders.name: Business owner
stakeholders.text: Pays for the platform and weighs what could be lost, in plain words.
concerns: Each view shows only what its reader needs

concerns.name: Each view shows only what its reader needs
concerns.text: The answer leads every view, the seal is always shown, and protocol detail reaches only the readers who act on it.

components.name: Prism page
components.text: The published GitHub Pages site: it checks the holo seal, sends the request to the verified guest in the browser and shows the answer in the reader's view.

quality.text: Every view renders the answer as a verdict card.
quality.measureText: Viewpoints for which the answer surface is not shown as a verdict card.

quality.text: Every view shows the holo seal.
quality.measureText: Viewpoints for which the seal surface is not a seal badge.

threats.name: Protocol detail buries the answer
threats.text: A leader handed rule traces misreads a hold as a no-go and stops a rollout that was safe.

control.name: Proved views
control.text: The leader view never renders a rule trace, proved for every request; the business view leaves rules out by its own rule, checked by its example.
